preamble: Half the solutions are to be entered in a 10 across manner. Ambiguities about some entries are resolved by the appearance of four names with something in common appearing in the completed grid..

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: French department's holding posh shields

indicators.note: something holding another thing has it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the Gard is a department in southern France, with the possessive S
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A wealthy French region keeps something protected behind armour.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's is part of the letters: GARD'S takes U inside to make GUARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard is to protect, which is what shields means as a verb.

clue.text: Place to learn language, including verb and everything

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so a letter is placed inside the combined pieces

parts.note: short for university
standard abbreviation for verb
Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: A school teaching a language covers grammar and all the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' works on the two joined pieces, so the verb letter lands exactly at their seam.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is the whole of existence, all there is.

clue.text: Follower of Attlee is left-leaning

indicators.note: leaning means tilted out of true, so the preceding letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone loyal to the Labour Prime Minister Clement Attlee has socialist sympathies.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives SATELLITE, which the preamble's revolutionary rule enters backwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite is a hanger-on or dependent that trails after someone more powerful.

clue.text: Winner almost failing with stratagems, it's said

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing

indicators.note: it's said points to how a word sounds rather than how it is written

parts.note: stratagems are tricks

explanation.surface: A champion nearly lost but resorted to cunning tactics, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Victrix is the Latin feminine of victor, as in Victoria Victrix.
explanation.definitionFit: Victrix is Latin for a female conqueror, so it names a winner.

clue.text: Businesses are providing drink

parts.note: CO for company, twice for the plural
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Firms are the ones supplying the refreshments.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives COCOA, entered backwards under the preamble's rule. The are is 100 square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate beverage.

clue.text: Destroy scripture that's in fashion

indicators.note: in places one thing within the other

parts.note: the rage is the current fashion, as in all the rage
the Authorized Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A command to wipe out holy writings that have become trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Authorized Version is the King James Bible, a standard crossword source of two letters for scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravage is to devastate or lay waste.

clue.text: Killer with hard axes, one leader in army — it could be lethal

parts.note: the asp is a venomous snake
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
Y and X are the two axes of a graph
Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of army

explanation.surface: A murderer armed with heavy axes and a lone officer makes a deadly combination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' are not choppers but graph axes, Y and X. The clue gives ASPHYXIA, entered backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphyxia, suffocation from lack of oxygen, is often fatal.

clue.text: Extremely insalubrious brown animal not back in city

indicators.note: without its back end, the word loses its final letter
extremely points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of insalubrious
tan is a light brown
a bull is an animal

explanation.surface: A grubby brown beast in an urban street, oddly unable to turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives ISTANBUL, entered backwards under the preamble's rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is Turkey's largest city, on the Bosphorus.

clue.text: Novel about trouble for Eastern leader

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the title is read from the far end

parts.note: Kim is Rudyard Kipling's novel
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A book about the problems facing an Asian ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an anagram signal but is the Kipling title. The clue gives MIKADO, entered backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado was a title for the Emperor of Japan, a ruler in the Far East.

clue.text: Voyeur on trial, criminal in novel

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A peeping Tom stands in the dock as the villain of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble's '10 across manner' means entered in a revolutionary way, i.e. turned round: half the answers go in backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something revolutionary is radically new, as a novel idea is.

clue.text: Story about neighbouring lives to set straight in a series

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the others

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
near means close by
is means exists, lives

explanation.surface: A tale about the lives of the people next door, told to put things in order.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's answer is entered backwards under the preamble's revolutionary rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To linearise is to arrange things in a line, one after another.

clue.text: Vehicle in recess reversing with velocity

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the combined letters are read the other way

parts.note: an apse is a vaulted recess in a church
v is the symbol for velocity

explanation.surface: A car backing out of an alcove at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: APSE plus V, all read backwards, gives the answer, which is entered forwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vespa is an Italian motor scooter, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Journo and merchant speaking in underground room

parts.note: a sub is a sub-editor on a newspaper

indicators.note: speaking means the word is heard rather than seen in writing

parts.note: a merchant is a seller

explanation.surface: A reporter and a trader talking in a basement.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives SUBCELLAR, entered backwards under the preamble's rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A subcellar is a cellar below another cellar, a room below ground.

clue.text: Return of one of the 1 having ID

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: 1 down is the guards; a gateman guards an entrance

explanation.surface: A guard coming back must show his identification.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal is in the wordplay itself, so this answer is entered forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A name tag is a badge identifying its wearer.

clue.text: Monkey around repeatedly in lake

parts.note: the titi is a small South American monkey
CA, for circa, meaning around, twice

explanation.surface: An ape swims in circles in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives TITICACA, entered backwards under the preamble's rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Titicaca is the large lake on the border of Peru and Bolivia.

clue.text: Shake with unease, ultimately retreating untrained for combat

parts.note: to wag is to shake, as a tail

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of unease

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: raw means inexperienced

explanation.surface: Trembling nervously, a raw recruit backs away from battle.
explanation.walkthrough: WAG and E, then RAW read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To wage war is to fight, to engage in combat as a verb.

clue.text: Self-destructive person back from brink — risk regularly accepted in shock

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of brink

indicators.note: accepted in means taken inside something else

parts.note: to amaze is to astound or shock

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of risk

explanation.surface: A daredevil pulled back from the edge, a dangerous gamble meeting with dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives KAMIKAZE, entered backwards under the preamble's rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Kamikaze pilots flew suicide missions, so the word names anyone recklessly self-destructive.

clue.text: Eyes may be tense, two drugs getting knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means sent backwards, so all the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
E for ecstasy and speed for amphetamine

explanation.surface: A tense user downs two drugs, eyes glazing over.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase to be completed: eyes may be deep-set. The whole string is reversed within the wordplay, so the entry goes in forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-set eyes are sunk well into the face, a common description of eyes.

clue.text: Island country hasn't deserted capital

indicators.note: hasn't means lacks, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a land is a country
D is an abbreviation for deserted
A1 means first-rate, capital; the 1 becomes I

explanation.surface: An island nation has not abandoned its seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city but is the exclamation of approval, A1. The clue gives LANAI, a Hawaiian island, entered backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanai is one of the islands of Hawaii.

clue.text: Heavenly object I put in place of worship

indicators.note: put in means placed inside something else

parts.note: an altar is a place of worship in a church
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets a sacred object down in a shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly' fits the religious surface but here means in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila.

clue.text: When travelling, atlas gets used and abused

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters move into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A road atlas gets battered on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives ASSAULTED, entered backwards under the preamble's rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To be assaulted is to be attacked or physically mistreated.

clue.text: Did forward line watch?

parts.note: to forward a letter is to send it on
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Did the front line keep guard?
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like a football position but is the verb send on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry keeps watch, and a watch is also the person on guard.

clue.text: Bird loves to be by grass

parts.note: grass and pot are both slang for cannabis
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O; two of them

explanation.surface: A bird that adores sitting beside the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The grass piece comes before the loves although the clue names them in the other order.
explanation.definitionFit: The potoo is a nocturnal bird of tropical America.

clue.text: Brooding opening piece, involving piano

parts.note: an intro is an opening

indicators.note: involving means wrapping something up within, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: a section is a piece
P is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A moody overture to a piano piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brooding opening' reads as one phrase, but the first word is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Introspection is looking inward at one's own thoughts, a form of brooding.

clue.text: Start with surprised expression to fix home

parts.note: O is a cry of surprise
to rig is to fix dishonestly
being in is being at home

explanation.surface: Begin with a startled look and set about repairing the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives ORIGIN, entered backwards under the preamble's rule.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the beginning or source of something.

clue.text: Start of trumpeting to encourage half-hearted angel

indicators.note: half-hearted means the heart is cut in half, so one of the two central letters goes
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of trumpeting
to reassure is to encourage

explanation.surface: A trumpet fanfare to rouse a hesitant heavenly being.
explanation.walkthrough: REASSURE has SS at its heart; losing one leaves REASURE. The clue gives TREASURE, entered backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure and angel are both terms of endearment for a beloved, helpful person.
